newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair to start its own cargo division.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair to start its own cargo division.

text.p: HONG KONG, Apr 21. (Reuter) Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) is to set up its own dedicated cargo division and put a much bigger emphasis on freight to increase revenue, the carrier's new chief executive officer, Stanley Hui told reporters.

"In Hong Kong, Cathay has always been the general sales agent for cargo but looking at the cargo volume we are now handling we've decided that we should strengthen our own capability and gradually set up our own Hong Kong cargo sales department with distribution and space control from the middle of the year to take our own cargo business further," Hui told reporters.

The former head of the territory's all-cargo airline, Air Hong Kong, said he was "very positive" about Dragonair's future and expected cargo revenue, which up to now has been a small part of the airline's revenue, to increase significantly.
Earlier, another senior Dragnnair executive, Augustus Tang, planning and international affairs general manager said cargo revenue would "soon more than double."

Dragonair is not a listed airline and does not publish its financial results. Officials did not reveal the current size of cargo revenue. Airline figures show it carried 17,413 tonnes of cargo in 1995 and 23,884 tonnes between January and November last year.

"Cargo was basically nothing when we operated 737s five years ago which were carrying 500 kilos. Now our Airbus A320s can carry four tonnes and our A330s around 24 tonnes so if we have two A330s a day into Shanghai that is one Boeing 707 freighter. It speaks for itself that we are certainly focussing on cargo, particularly as we have not done much in the past," Hui said.
In another move which is expected to boost profitability, Dragonair has been granted permission within the past six weeks to issue its own airway bills in China.

"Up to now restrictions have been imposed on the way we can distribute cargo in China and sell our product. We have not been able to issue our own airway bills and had to use local airlines in China for distribution. Now that's all changed," Tang said.
Dragonair has also applied to China's aviation regulatory body, CAAC, for permission to issue tickets in China, Tang said.

Dragonair is increasingly benefitting from Beijing's support and last year's change of ownership when the China National Aviation Corporation (CNAC) took over the majority shareholding from Cathay Pacific Airways Limited.

The new cargo division was another example of the Dragonair's 'coming of age,' establishing itself in its own right but also its increasing distance from former owner Cathay Pacific, the observers added.
Hui said Dragonair was changing but Cathay remains an important partner.

"We are saying we are not doing everything on our own. We have always cooperated very closely with Cathay in practical areas like computer reservation system, aircraft maintenance and they are also our world-wide general sales agent for both passengers and cargo so that sort of relationship with Cathay will definitely continue," Hui said.

Main Dragonair shareholders are China National Aviation Corp with some 36 percent, CITIC Pacific Ltd with 28 percent whilst Swire Pacific Ltd and Cathay Pacific jointly hold a further 26 percent. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
